Shipwrecks.notes: Nathan Henry, Assistant State Archaeologist and Conservator from the NC Office of State Archaeology, said the following about this strange piece of debris., "That's the side of a pretty large, late 19th-early 20th century wooden Sailing Vessel. It was probably one of the larger ones with 5-6 masts. It seems one of the larger ones Ran Aground on Hatteras shoals and was destroyed as a hazard to navigation--early 20th century. The frag[ment]s ended up near the pony pens and have been there ever since. Anyway, there have been some pretty large chunks uncovered over the years. Undoubtedly it was uncovered and did not wash up. It will cover up again. This piece looks to incorporate the framework just above the turn-of-the-bilge (waterward)--at least that is what is visible. There may be more to it beneath the sediment on the water side."
